tools.description:
Clear a record's subject exclusion, so a label match may link the concept again. A NO is durable, not
permanent — without this one wrong tap would make a record permanently un-linkable to a concept, with
nothing on screen to say why the classifier kept ignoring it.
tools.name: semantic_about_after_all

tools.description:
Ask a named question, e.g. semantic_ask('goals_realized_by_components_on_node',
{'node': 'M1'}) -> which goals are transitively realized by components on that node.
tools.name: semantic_ask

tools.description:
Assert a classified facet (document_type | owner | sensitivity_label | projection_url | rendering) at a provenance
rung: the row's column AND the graph triple with its PROV record. Owner and label are refused anywhere
but C (NFR-3).
tools.name: semantic_catalog_assert

tools.description:
The Catalog row for the document ONE WEB URL names — the `https://...` address a person copies
out of a browser, or that a search result or a citation gives — or null when no record is held
for it. Same shape as `semantic_catalog_get`: identity and custody, never content.

This is how a question about a document somebody is LOOKING at ("who owns this, is it approved,
what does it affect") reaches the governed record. null means exactly that no catalogued artifact
has that url's custody — it is never the record with the nearest title, because two records
sharing a title is precisely the case a title match gets wrong and nobody can see it has.

The url is resolved by the PROVIDER through the governed collaboration port, not from an index of
the fabric's own: a web url is path-based, so renaming or moving a file changes it while the item
it names does not (`lab.substrate.fabric_custody` records the full reasoning).
tools.name: semantic_catalog_by_url

tools.description:
The Catalog row for an artifact — by IRI, or by POINTER ({source, handle|ref|…}) — plus its graph
links by rung (delivery, references, subjects, facets), or null. Identity and custody only — never content.
tools.name: semantic_catalog_get

tools.description:
One page of the catalogue in IRI order — {items:[{iri,title,document_type,state,pointer,…}], cursor,
more}. Pass `cursor` straight back as `after` to continue; never compose one yourself.

KEYSET, not offset: rows are added while a long walk runs, so an offset would silently skip or repeat
records. `state` narrows to one lifecycle state and refuses one that does not exist, because a typo
returning an empty page is the one answer an operator would act on wrongly. Metadata only, as ever.
tools.name: semantic_catalog_list

tools.description:
Re-read ONE catalogued artifact with today's classifier — {request_id, duplicate, pointer}.

You name a record; you supply NOTHING else. The pointer, the producing process and the delivery
context all come from the row the fabric itself recorded, so this cannot introduce an input the lab
has not already validated. That is what makes it legitimate for a process whose `submit` deliberately
does not exist (`ARTIFACT_INTAKE.external = False` — the ArtifactChanged event IS the provenance of
everything a normal run records), and it is the same argument `workflow_replay` makes: a caller may
ask that inputs already accepted be used again, never supply new ones.

The run carries `reason=reclassify`, so it re-links the subjects and asks NOBODY unless the record
gains a document type — re-reading a back catalogue must not raise a second card for every record
whose first one is still open.

An artifact whose pointer names nothing is refused rather than submitted: intake reads the artifact
THROUGH its pointer, so a row without one is not a thing that can be re-read, and spending a run to
discover that would read as a classifier fault rather than a catalogue one.
tools.name: semantic_catalog_reclassify

tools.description:
Move an artifact's lifecycle (pending | in-review | published | withdrawn), optionally recording the
baseline version and whether it is unassociated with any delivery context.
tools.name: semantic_catalog_state

tools.description:
Identify an artifact: mint its IRI (or find it by pointer) and mirror the row into rung C. A lab
process's output (`produced_by`) gets its document type as a FACT and its delivery edge from the run's
`context` (`<kind>:<id>`). Idempotent on the pointer.
tools.name: semantic_catalog_upsert

tools.description:
Is `relation` permitted from element type `source` to `target`? Exact answer from the
ArchiMate relationship matrix, plus the full list of what is allowed for that pair.
tools.name: semantic_check

tools.description:
Candidate element types for a concept described in words (e.g. 'REST API exposed by
the backend'). Deterministic keyword scoring — the agent makes the final call using the
definitions returned.
tools.name: semantic_classify

tools.description:
Which concept a TERM means — matched against concept DEFINITIONS, for a term whose words matched
no label. The semantic tier of the inverted classifier: `{term, concept, label, score, margin,
scheme, unavailable}`, where an empty `concept` is the ORDINARY answer.

Nothing is not a failure. Measured 17 Oct 2026 on real documents, 19 of 30 extracted terms matched
no concept confidently, and the ones refused include `dead-letter handling rota -> Migration
disposition` — nonsense an absolute score threshold would have accepted. A term that falls through
becomes a candidate for a steward, which is how the vocabulary learns what the corpus needed and it
did not have.

`unavailable` is NOT a miss: it means no embedder is configured, so the question could not be asked
at all. "The vocabulary has no such concept" is a claim about the corpus; "I could not ask" is a
claim about the deployment, and reading one as the other would make an outage look like a
vocabulary gap.

It INDEXES lazily — definitions not yet in the embedder's space are embedded on the way past, which
is why it is a pipeline verb and not a read.
tools.name: semantic_concept_match

tools.description:
Concepts the CORPUS keeps connecting that the vocabulary says nothing about.

Two concepts turning up on the same documents again and again is the corpus saying they are related;
a vocabulary silent about them has a gap a steward can close. Evidence, never a conclusion —
co-occurrence is not a relation and cannot name one, so this proposes the QUESTION and a person
answers it. Read at the trusted rungs, so a model's suggestion never proposes a relation. Counts and
concept ids, never content.
tools.name: semantic_concept_pairs

tools.description:
Concepts of a scheme: the whole vocabulary, or the subtree under `root_label` (e.g. 'Patient Management')
to `depth` levels. Kinds in a capability map: capability, value-stream, org-unit, stakeholder, information.
Pass an EMPTY kind for every kind at once, which is what a domain ontology needs — its concepts are entities,
references and events, and asking for one of them would silently return part of the vocabulary.
tools.name: semantic_concepts

tools.description:
Rebuild the DERIVED rung (D) from the trusted rungs: an artifact is related to the context of what it
references; a record synthesised from minutes inherits their context. Counts only; impact reads D.
tools.name: semantic_derive

tools.description:
Classification card for an element type: layer, aspect (active/behaviour/passive),
definition, examples, and what it is commonly confused with.
tools.name: semantic_describe

tools.description:
Enter one edge at a rung (S needs a confidence; D is computed, never asserted). SHACL-checked: a
content property never enters. `supersede` retracts the subject's previous value of that predicate.
tools.name: semantic_edge_assert

tools.description: Supersede an edge (PROV invalidation — never deleted). `actor` names the person or the rule.
tools.name: semantic_edge_retract

tools.description:
Index an artifact by its DESCRIPTIVE text (title · type · subjects) through the gateway embedder.
Never a body: the index proposes neighbours, it stores no content.
tools.name: semantic_embed

tools.description:
Project a reference scheme (or subtree) to an ArchiMate model spec — Capability /
ValueStream elements with Composition, plus an L1 overview view and one nested view per
top concept. Feed the result to the EA-repository server's archimate_render + ea_stage_import:
that is the governed way to write reference capabilities into the EA repository.
By default the spec is stored as an artifact and only counts + spec_ref (art://…) are
returned — the gateway meters tool payloads as tokens and ea-mcp accepts spec_ref from
any host. by_ref=False returns the payload inline (small subtrees); out_path also writes a
local copy (dev).
tools.name: semantic_export_archimate

tools.description:
What a change to this artifact may have invalidated: everything reaching it over the delivery and
reference axes on TRUSTED rungs (C·X·H·D — never S, NFR-7), joined with the catalog.
tools.name: semantic_impact

tools.description:
Load a model into the semantic store as RDF (with derived relationships) so it can be queried
with semantic_query / semantic_ask.

Pass the spec by value (`spec`) or by artifact reference (`spec_ref`, art://…), exactly as
semantic_validate_model does. The reference is what a WORKLOAD must use: it holds no store
credentials, so a spec it produced is already an art:// ref and cannot be passed any other way.

NOTE the store is IN-MEMORY and per process: what is loaded here is queryable for the life of
this server and does not survive a restart or reach a second replica. Keep the durable copy as
an artifact (semantic_store_spec) and reload it when it is needed.
tools.name: semantic_load_model

tools.description:
The fabric's published measurements (BR-8), as last computed by the reconciler's tick: auto-association
ratio, drafts approved without rewrite, impact notices acknowledged, duplicate rate, labelled and owned
share — each with its numerator and denominator. Numbers, never content.
tools.name: semantic_metrics

tools.description:
Record that a PERSON says this record is NOT about this concept, and retract the subject.

Durable, which is the point: retracting alone left no trace, so the next classification matched the same
label and put the subject straight back — a `keep` lasted for ever and a `drop` lasted until the next
sweep. The sibling of `semantic_vocab_decline`, one level down: that one is a person's NO about a TERM,
this is a person's NO about one RECORD. `semantic_about_after_all` clears it.
tools.name: semantic_not_about

tools.description: Vocabularies available in the semantic layer and their sizes.
tools.name: semantic_ontologies

tools.description:
A PERSON moves an assertion up the ladder (default to H): with a predicate and object, that edge;
with the subject alone, a candidate concept is accepted. `actor` is the signed-in human — blank is refused.
tools.name: semantic_promote

tools.description:
Run SPARQL across the vocabularies and every loaded model. Prefixes:
am: <urn:lab:semantic:archimate#>  meta: <urn:lab:semantic:meta#>. Derived relations
are am:derivedRealization / am:derivedServing / am:derivedAssignment / ...
tools.name: semantic_query

tools.description: Named traceability questions available to semantic_ask, with their parameters.
tools.name: semantic_questions

tools.description:
Before you create a document: the PUBLISHED records already on this topic, each with its owner and source
pointer — reuse or ask instead of writing a twin. Never content.
tools.name: semantic_recommend

tools.description:
Embed every catalog row the current embedder's space lacks, from its facets (title · type · subjects).
What a switched embedder costs: one call. Counts only.
tools.name: semantic_reindex

tools.description:
What else the corpus is ABOUT this record — ranked by the RAREST concept the two share, each row naming
that concept so a reader can check the rank.

The complement of `semantic_similar`, which proposes neighbours from an embedding of a record's facets and
so answers "what reads like this". This reads asserted subjects on the trusted rungs only, so a model's
suggestion never ranks as a relation. Rarest, not most: two records sharing five concepts that everything
shares have said nothing, and a count would rank them above one exact match — and a concept the WHOLE corpus
carries relates nobody, so it is left out rather than padding the answer.

TWO KINDS of neighbour, `via_kind` on every row. `shared` — about a concept in common, the stronger
evidence. `derived` — about NO concept in common, but about concepts the vocabulary states are related
("a document about Prescription and a spreadsheet about Prescription item"), read from rung D and
reported with the predicate that joins them (`via_predicate`, `via_object`). Shared ranks above derived
always; within a kind, the rarer concept wins. A derived neighbour exists only once the derivation has
run, which happens on a publish — a record that has never been published has none.

A withdrawn record is hidden unless `state` asks for it, as in `semantic_search`. Facets and scores,
never content.
tools.name: semantic_related

tools.description:
Reference models loaded as SKOS concept schemes (capability maps, value streams,
organisation / stakeholder / information maps) with per-kind, per-level counts.
tools.name: semantic_schemes

tools.description:
The facade: similarity over the index filtered by catalog facets (document type, lifecycle state).
Withdrawn records are hidden unless `state="withdrawn"` is asked for.
tools.name: semantic_search
semantic_similar

tools.description:
Store a text document (Markdown, HTML) in the artifact store AS ITSELF and return its art:// ref.

The sibling of `semantic_store_spec`, and not the same tool: a spec is JSON and is stored as JSON, while a
page must arrive at its reader byte for byte — `{"text": "# Title"}` written into a wiki is a file nobody
can read. The content type comes from the NAME, so a caller cannot mislabel its own file.
tools.name: semantic_store_page

tools.description:
Store a model spec (the archimate_render / semantic_validate_model JSON) in the artifact
store and return its art:// reference plus counts. Lets a workload keep its intermediate
spec BY REFERENCE without holding store credentials itself — the deterministic workflow
node calls this through the gateway. Writes only to the artifact store (never to the EA
repository), so it needs no human approval.
tools.name: semantic_store_spec

tools.description:
Draw what this record is about and what that connects it to, AS THE GRAPH STANDS NOW, and store the
drawing — returns {ref, name, media_type, suffix, nodes, edges, concepts, statuses, title}.

The drawing is named in the RENDERER's own terms (`suffix`, `media_type`) and never as HTML: which adapter
draws is configuration (`FABRIC_RENDERER`), so a caller that assumed a page would break the day a raster or
an interactive one is configured — the one change the renderer registry exists to make free.

Every call rebuilds the view from the catalogue and the vocabulary, so a picture is never older than the
knowledge; there is no stored layout to go stale. The colour of each box is the RUNG the link was made at,
so the drawing answers how the fabric knows what it claims and not merely what it claims. `proposed` are
terms the record used that the vocabulary has no concept for — drawn as gaps, because a gap a person can
see is one a steward can close. Reading only: it writes an artifact, never the graph.
tools.name: semantic_topology

tools.description:
Breadth-first over the chosen rung graphs from `start`, joined with the catalog. The rungs you choose
ARE the trust policy of the answer; each hit carries the weakest rung on its path.
tools.name: semantic_trace

tools.description:
Validate a model spec (same JSON as archimate_render): every illegal relationship with
the allowed alternatives, plus semantic warnings such as services consumed without an
interface assigned to them. Pass the spec by value (`spec`) or by artifact reference
(`spec_ref`, art://…) — the reference keeps the tool argument small for agent callers.
tools.name: semantic_validate_model

tools.description:
Run the fabric's SHACL shapes over its graphs now (metadata-only, owner provenance, assertion
completeness) — the fitness function, on demand.
tools.name: semantic_validate_shapes

tools.description:
Step 22's views: the logical reference architecture and the physical reference
implementation, each showing ONLY the solution's scope (layers with nothing in scope
collapse to a strip). Returns `{logical_ref, physical_ref, summary, rules_source}`.

basename.description: The stored file's name, without extension.

components.description: The SELECTED components: catalogue ids (cmp-…) or codes (GW-02). Logical building blocks are derived from them.

field.description: The derived field the read is attributed to (e.g. `capability_view`).

pattern.description: P1–P5, when the solution follows one.

pin_id.description: The run's pin (reference_pin). A view reads the governed corpus under it and refuses without one.

process.description: The registered process the run belongs to.

run_id.description: The run the view is drawn for — recorded against the read.

title.description: The page title — the use case's problem, in a few words.

use_case.description: The use case's id, printed under the title.

tools.name: semantic_view_architecture

tools.description:
Step 5's view: the whole technology capability map with every impacted L3 filled —
red missing, green new, amber consumed (C) or updated (U) — and the rest faded. Stores
one HTML page; returns `{html_ref, summary, rules_source}`. Unknown ids are listed on the
page and under `summary.unresolved`, never dropped.

basename.description: The stored file's name, without extension.

capabilities.description: Impacted technology L3s: {id, status: missing|new|consumed|updated, note?}; a capability NOT on the map is {name, parent_l2, status} and is drawn as a proposed block (a capability-map delta).

field.description: The derived field the read is attributed to (e.g. `capability_view`).

pin_id.description: The run's pin (reference_pin). A view reads the governed corpus under it and refuses without one.

process.description: The registered process the run belongs to.

run_id.description: The run the view is drawn for — recorded against the read.

title.description: The page title — the use case's problem, in a few words.

use_case.description: The use case's id, printed under the title.

tools.name: semantic_view_capabilities

tools.description:
Draw the WHOLE catalogue — every record that is about something, the concepts they share, and the
vocabulary's own edges between those — and store the drawing. Returns the same shape as
`semantic_topology` plus `records`/`silent`.

The question it answers is the one no per-record picture can: what is our knowledge ABOUT, and what is
it silent on. Resolved in process, deliberately — a caller walking the catalogue over the gateway pays
a round trip per record and trips its own rate limit at about sixty.

`state` narrows to one lifecycle state (an unknown one is refused, so a typo never reads as "nothing
matched"); `limit` caps records READ. What is DRAWN is the view's decision: a record about nothing has
no edge, so it is counted in the subtitle rather than left on the rim saying nothing. Reading only.
tools.name: semantic_view_corpus

tools.description:
Step 9's view: the ontology match as an interactive force-directed page (offline — the
script is inlined). Green matched, amber partial or enhancement, red gap (the ontology
delta), grey context. Returns `{html_ref, summary, rules_source}`.

basename.description: The stored file's name, without extension.

concepts.description: Concepts the use case needs: {id (as in the ontology), status: matched|partial|enhancement|gap, note?}; a gap also gives {name, module, kind, definition}.

field.description: The derived field the read is attributed to (e.g. `capability_view`).

pin_id.description: The run's pin (reference_pin). A view reads the governed corpus under it and refuses without one.

process.description: The registered process the run belongs to.

relationships.description: Relationships the use case adds or changes: {subject, predicate, object, status?}. Existing ones between matched concepts are added automatically.

run_id.description: The run the view is drawn for — recorded against the read.

title.description: The page title — the use case's problem, in a few words.

use_case.description: The use case's id, printed under the title.

tools.name: semantic_view_ontology

tools.description:
Step 6's view: the realisation view with the shortlisted L3s filled by status and the
chosen route marked ✔. UAE North availability shows as grey glyphs so the fill is the only
colour. Returns `{html_ref, summary, rules_source}`.

basename.description: The stored file's name, without extension.

field.description: The derived field the read is attributed to (e.g. `capability_view`).

pin_id.description: The run's pin (reference_pin). A view reads the governed corpus under it and refuses without one.

process.description: The registered process the run belongs to.

realisations.description: Shortlisted realisations: {id (L3), status: missing|new|consumed|updated, route?: microsoft|sovereign|alternative, product?, note?}.

run_id.description: The run the view is drawn for — recorded against the read.

title.description: The page title — the use case's problem, in a few words.

use_case.description: The use case's id, printed under the title.

tools.name: semantic_view_realisations

tools.description:
Step 10's view: the workflow as BPMN swimlanes whose tasks are L3 capabilities. Unknown
lanes or node ids are refused by name. Returns `{html_ref, summary, rules_source}`.

basename.description: The stored file's name, without extension.

field.description: The derived field the read is attributed to (e.g. `capability_view`).

pin_id.description: The run's pin (reference_pin). A view reads the governed corpus under it and refuses without one.

process.description: The registered process the run belongs to.

run_id.description: The run the view is drawn for — recorded against the read.

spec.description: The flow: {title, lanes: [{id, label}], nodes: [{id, type: task|gateway|start|end|annotation, lane, cap?, name?, note?}], edges: [{from, to, type?, label?}]}. A task naming only `cap` (an L3 id) is labelled from the pinned map.

tools.name: semantic_view_workflow

tools.description:
Teach a concept the vocabulary ALREADY holds another name, so the next document using that term is
linked instead of proposing the same candidate again. The steward's answer to "this term has no concept"
when it does, under a different name — admitting a second would be the duplicate this prevents.
tools.name: semantic_vocab_amend

tools.description:
Record that a steward has ALREADY BEEN ASKED about this term, so the next tick does not ask again.

`fab:InReview`, the word the lifecycle already had. Kept in the REGISTER rather than in the memory of
whichever process asked: that memory was a set, it emptied on every restart, and the open cards went
from 71 to 101 in one afternoon while nobody decided anything. Idempotent — a candidate already asked
about, admitted or declined is left exactly as it is, and says so.
tools.name: semantic_vocab_asked

tools.description:
The AUTHOR's answer about a term extracted from their document: `confirm` sends it to a steward,
`rename` corrects the word first (give `label`), `remove` withdraws it — recorded as withdrawn by the
author, not declined by a steward. `actor` is the signed-in author; blank is refused. Answered once.
tools.name: semantic_vocab_author_confirm

tools.description:
Terms a run met that the vocabulary has no concept for and nobody has accepted or declined yet — what
a steward is asked to admit, place under another name, or decline.
tools.name: semantic_vocab_candidates

tools.description:
Seed the candidate register from another master's decisions — the HANDOVER, so a steward is never
asked twice about a term or a relation they already answered elsewhere.

Each row is a TERM `{label, scheme, status, actor?, reason?, proposed_for?}` or a RELATION
`{scheme, subject, predicate, object, status, actor?, reason?}`; `status` is Pending | Withdrawn |
Admitted, words or ids are both fine. A row's `actor` is who DECIDED; `actor` here is the operator
running the import (required). Idempotent. `Admitted` is checked against the vocabulary (admissions
travel in the master) and reported, never parked. Returns {imported, results, problems}.
tools.name: semantic_vocab_candidates_import

tools.description:
Words this vocabulary gives more than one meaning, which no document could therefore be linked to.
A steward settles each by retiring one meaning or renaming it; until then the link is not made, because
linking to both is worse than linking to neither.
tools.name: semantic_vocab_conflicts

tools.description:
Record a STEWARD'S NO about a candidate term, so nobody is asked about it again.

The decline used to live only on the approval, while the reconciler's "already asked" memory is a set in
the PROCESS — so every restart re-asked every still-open candidate with a fresh approval id. Measured
10 Oct 2026: the open concept-admission cards went from 71 to 101 in one afternoon while a steward
decided nothing. A person's answer has to outlive the process that heard it.

`actor` is the person, never an agent name — this is a decision about what the fabric will mean for every
document classified from now on. The term may be met again; it will not be asked about again.
tools.name: semantic_vocab_decline

tools.description:
Link an artifact to every reference concept whose preferred label a term matches exactly (rung X,
method label-match). Misses are returned for semantic_vocab_propose.
tools.name: semantic_vocab_link

tools.description:
Render the vocabulary as its human-readable MASTER and store it by reference — what an operator then
signs and publishes into the governed corpus.

Returns {artifact_id: {ref, name, rows, command}}. It stages; it does not publish, and it cannot: the
signing seed is off every service by design and the corpus reader holds SELECT only. The `command` is the
exact line to run. The master is the SOURCE — the publisher hashes this text and derives its records from
parsing it, so `derived_from = master_sha256` is mechanical rather than a promise.
tools.name: semantic_vocab_master

tools.description:
Put an admitted concept UNDER a broader one — or, with an empty parent, back at the root.

The vocabulary's topology, as against its membership. `broader` is settable only at proposal time and the
steward's batch card deliberately collects no parent, so a concept arrives unplaced and the hierarchy
froze at admission: this is how it gets organised afterwards, which is when somebody usually knows where a
concept belongs. A cycle is refused by name rather than hanging the next reader, and a retired concept is
refused at either end. `actor` is the signed-in steward and is required.
tools.name: semantic_vocab_place

tools.description:
Park a candidate concept for a steward. Not in any scheme until a person accepts it (semantic_promote
with the candidate's IRI and no predicate), at which point it IS admitted and findable from then on.
`scheme` is the vocabulary it would join and `concept_id` the id it would take — the steward supplies
whichever is missing at the gate, because a concept with no home cannot be looked up.

`proposed_for` is the ARTIFACT whose words proposed the term. There is ONE row per term and this is
accumulated onto it, so a steward is asked once however many documents want the word, the count of
them is the evidence of whether it matters, and admitting it re-matches exactly those artifacts
instead of the whole catalogue. Omit it and the candidate is parked with no provenance: the frequency
threshold reads a count that is then always null and asks about every term on first sight, and
admission propagates to nothing.

`alias_of` is the concept a matcher thinks this term is another WORD FOR, when the semantic tier
found one. It is a suggestion recorded on the candidate, never a write to the vocabulary — amending
a scheme is a steward's act behind the PROMOTE grant. It turns the card's expensive question ("what
does this mean, and where does it sit?") into the cheap one ("is this another word for X?").
tools.name: semantic_vocab_propose

tools.description:
State how two concepts are connected, with a TYPED predicate.

`skos:related` cannot carry what the derived rung needs — "A is about X, X relates to Y, B is about Y" is
answerable only if the edge names its predicate — so a steward's relation arrives in the same shape as the
vocabulary's own and publishes through the relationships master unchanged. A dangling end, a retired end,
a self-relation and a duplicate are each refused by name. `actor` is the signed-in steward and is required.
tools.name: semantic_vocab_relate

tools.description:
What a structured diagram proposes about the vocabulary's TOPOLOGY, resolved against it.

`arrows` are a parsed diagram's connectors — `{"from": <box text>, "to": <box text>, "label": <arrow text>}`,
the shape `storage_read_vsdx` already returns. The boxes are terms and the arrows are relations, which makes
a diagram the one artifact carrying how the things a corpus is about are CONNECTED rather than just which
they are.

Returns `{candidates, gaps, scheme}`. A box the vocabulary cannot name is a GAP, not an error — it is a
term a steward can admit, and dropping it silently is how a diagram stops being evidence. An AMBIGUOUS box
resolves to nothing: choosing between two meanings narrows the vocabulary, which no diagram may settle. An
unlabelled arrow is a candidate marked `unnamed` — the diagram says two concepts connect, not how, and a
guessed predicate is an edge no author drew.

Read-only. It proposes; a steward writes with `semantic_vocab_relate`.
tools.name: semantic_vocab_relation_candidates

tools.description:
A PERSON says these two concepts are not related that way — recorded so it sticks.

The sibling of `semantic_vocab_decline`. Both producers recompute their candidates on every run, so
without a durable NO the same question comes back for ever.
tools.name: semantic_vocab_relation_decline

tools.description:
Relation questions still waiting on a steward — what the ontology queue asks about.

Openness is DERIVED: a question disappears exactly when the vocabulary STATES the relation, however
it came to, and a declined one stays gone. So the queue cannot drift from the vocabulary it is a
queue for, and no path has to remember to clean up after itself.
tools.name: semantic_vocab_relation_open

tools.description:
Park a question about how two concepts RELATE, for a steward to answer.

Idempotent on (scheme, subject, predicate case-folded, object), so two producers proposing the same
relation — a diagram's arrows and the corpus's co-occurrences — raise ONE question. `evidence` is what
a steward triages on ("3 documents are about both", "drawn on the eRx context diagram"). It parks a
QUESTION, never a relation: `semantic_vocab_relate` is the write, and it takes a person's name.

`subject`/`object` may be WORDS — a concept's label or alt label — resolved by the vocabulary, an
ambiguous or unknown word refused naming the choices. `actor` is who proposed it (a person, or the
system acting for one) and `proposed_for` the catalogue IRI of the artifact that proposed it; both
accumulate on the one question, and `semantic_vocab_relation_open` returns them.
tools.name: semantic_vocab_relation_propose

tools.description:
The classifier's subject match as ONE decision: link every term whose preferred label matches
(rung X), ask what each MISS means against concept definitions, and park whatever is left as a
candidate for a steward — `proposed_for` this artifact, carrying `alias_of` when the semantic tier
recognised it as another word for a concept already held.

Answers with the link result whole — `linked`, `missed`, `retracted`, `excluded`, `conflicts` — plus
`proposed`, one entry per parked term. Use this rather than calling semantic_vocab_link,
semantic_concept_match and semantic_vocab_propose in turn: the order and the failure rules are the
fabric's, and a semantic tier that is unavailable costs only the suggestion, never the term.

`awaiting_author`: the terms were EXTRACTED from the artifact, so each parked term first waits for the
artifact's author (state `awaiting-author`, answered with semantic_vocab_author_confirm) before a
steward is asked.
tools.name: semantic_vocab_resolve

tools.description:
Supersede a concept: it stops being offered to classifiers and keeps RESOLVING to the one that replaced
it. Never deleted — a link made last month names the old id, and a lookup that fails on it turns a correct
historical statement into a dangling one. `actor` is the signed-in human; blank is refused.
tools.name: semantic_vocab_retire
